### introDuction **•** **_July is likely to see all the precious metal markets start to develop a base ahead of gains that could exceed 20% by yearend. Silver’s volatile nature and the gold:silver relationship suggest that an investment-driven rally in gold in the final quarter of 2012 could easily be outpaced by silver, especially if silver speculators, until now bruised by the falls experienced in 2011, regain their nerve._** **•** **_There are tentative signs of a shift in the nature of activity in gold and this, along with other analysis, suggests that gold is, to some extent, re-acquiring its role as a safe haven. Gold is expected to form a base in July ahead of strengthening in the rest of the third quarter, an acceleration in the final three months and a clearance of $1,900 in the first quarter of 2013. This may yet be a conservative view, especially if the markets start to focus on the problems in the United States and the need to take action to avoid overt economic weakness._** **•** **_There was a subtle, but potentially important, change in sentiment in the silver market also, with ETF investment returning and long-side Comex investors also adding positions. We expect consolidation mid-year and then fresh strength, driven by gold, in late 2012 and into 2013, producing a test of $50 next year with an average in the region of $42 in 2013 after just under $33 this year._**

**•** **_Platinum remains in a surplus, but the market is now unwinding oversold conditions after trading below $1,380 on an intra-day basis at the end of June. South African producer margins remain under pressure and some cuts in production have now been announced. While of themselves insufficient to throw platinum back into balance, the announcements have affected sentiment. We continue to expect platinum to benefit from renewed investment in the second half of this_** **_year, driven particularly by fresh interest in gold and by any signs, albeit tentative, of stabilisation in Europe. The price could therefore easily clear $1,700 before year-end._** **•** **_Palladium’s fundamentals are robust and the price was over-extended in late June. The weakness was largely a function of risk-aversion, with palladium falling with other metals and short-sided positions increasing on Nymex. Palladium will remain in a deficit, even prior to any investment activity, for the foreseeable future. ### GOLD 

**•** **_Gold’s rally at the start of June followed disappointing non-farm payroll figures in the United States, prompting fresh thoughts of potential fiscal stimulus, and boosting gold from below $1,550 to more than $1,600 in one day.  The fresh strength at the end of June followed the outcome of the EU summit.   The overall gradual uptrend in price since mid-May suggests that the market is starting to consolidate._** 

**•** **_We are looking for a challenge of at least $1,880 in the final quarter of the year.  This level could well be exceeded as there is a distinct probability of increased price volatility in late 2012, especially if investors’ attention turns, inter alia, to the US’ balance sheet and if the Eurozone finally seems to be approaching resolution to its debt problems.  A challenge of $1,950 in the first quarter of 2013 is a distinct possibility._** 

**•** **_With respect to the near-term downside, we expect a drift during mid-year due to investor uncertainty and a fractured physical market.  We are thus expecting renewed tests of $1,550 this month, but believe that this will be the low._** 

**•** **_There are hints that the tone is changing in the market as longer-term investors have been bargain hunting, with ETF investors taking a fresh interest in the market.  Investors on Comex have, as usual, been more volatile.  The cautious shift in the tone in the silver market would also suggest that these two metals are establishing a body of support that will bolster strength later this year._** 

There is time to establish long positions as market sentiment remains cautious overall, although some investors are already showing interest 

The strong price bounce at the start of June took gold out of the downtrend that had started at the end of February, triggered by reaction to a statement from Dr. Bernanke that the markets read as implying that there would be no further quantitative easing.  The top channel of that trend, which had previously been providing resistance, then became support for the price over the course of June.  It was also the springboard for the very sharp bounce at the end of the month following the outcome of the European summit, which helped to support the euro against the dollar while boosting investors’ risk appetite. 

It is likely that gold prices will drift lower during July in the face of physical weakness and continued uncertainty about whether gold is a risk asset or a safe haven, but there is  chart-based price support at $1,550.  Meanwhile, despite the recent bounce the longer-term downtrend that started in September 2011 has not been severed.  For this trend to be broken in July 2012, gold would have to trade towards $1,690 and we do not believe that this is likely. Severance of the downtrend by the end of August, however, would mean trading above $1,660 by month-end and  this latter alternative is certainly  feasible, as investors start to establish fresh hedges against currency volatil

After fluctuating over much of the month a late fall took it back down towards $1,540 before the end-month bounce that saw a test of $1,607. Major drivers in the market over June included: - **_The poor non-farm payrolls at the start of the month as the market response revolved around renewed thoughts of the possibility of further stimulus._** - **_(7th June); Dr. Bernanke’s testimony to lawmakers in which he urged Congress to address fiscal policy, arguing that “monetary policy is not a panacea”. The physical background and the implications for the coming weeks The physical gold market spent much of June characterised by patchy physical demand and intermittent, although declining, scrap flows. There were signs of improved demand towards month-end, but this was short-lived. on the Shanghai gold Exchange (SgE), turnover in the physical contracts remained lively during June. priceelasticity was still evident, with a fall in volume after the price rally at the start of June, but a strong boost in the wake of the price fall in mid-month. The average daily turnover for June was 7.5 tonnes, leading to a daily average of 8.3 tonnes for the first half of the year. The daily average for the first half of 2011, by comparison, was 8.0 tonnes, and for the year as a whole, was 7.7 tonnes. The average SgE premium over loco london during June was just 0.3%, however, compared with 0.6% for the first half of the year overall. Both of these sets of figures tend to confirm anecdotal evidence of plentiful domestic supply of metal feeding healthy demand.
